area: Fit of a /demo/ page, a two-minute video and a homepage tile with /home/user/labconstrictor-site (rules, generation, checks, weight)

facts.statement: Pages are generated as Markdown with front matter by the Page class; links are made relative to the page
facts.evidence: scripts/lcsite/page.py:232-276. fix_links (page.py:259-268) rewrites only href and src. build_site.py:66-91 calls clean(), media, hosts, home, apps, ecosystem, submit, guides.build, hubs.write_all, redirects, llms in that order.

facts.statement: A page highlights Docs in the top menu through the front-matter key menu: guides/, which overrides/main.html:35 compares with the nav item's url
facts.evidence: Used by hubs.py:84,98, guides.py:129 and pages_apps.py:192 (menu="apps/"). In my scratch build, Page("demo/index.md", menu="guides/", layout="wide") gave exactly one is-active entry (Docs) and check_site reported 39 pages, 0 problems. Without menu: check_site.menu_problems (check_site.py:132-135) fails. The Docs sidebar appears only if guide_nav is also set (main.html:54). Home's menu url is not needed.

facts.statement: The generated-file inventory is GENERATED in config.py:120-121 plus .gitignore; the README and AGENTS.md also list it by hand
facts.evidence: build_site.clean() (build_site.py:27-32) deletes each GENERATED entry. .gitignore ignores docs/index.md, apps/, guides/, use/, build/, ecosystem.md, submit.md, llms.txt, assets/{docs-img,icons,shots,images,hubs,hosts}. docs/assets/{fonts,javascripts,stylesheets} are tracked and authored (not generated). README.md ('Files under docs/ ...') and the AGENTS.md 'Generated and git-ignored' bullet repeat the list and need updating. No test cross-checks .gitignore against GENERATED.

facts.statement: Instant navigation is OFF, so every page is a full load; lc.js runs once per page and guards itself
facts.evidence: mkdocs.yml features are navigation.top, search.suggest, search.highlight only; built index.html __config lists the same; grep for 'instant' gives 0. lc.js:105-107 subscribes to document$ (defined by the bundle: window.document$) or DOMContentLoaded, and each init returns early when its element is absent (lcInitFilter, lcInitSystem). Its comment about 'instant navigation' is stale.

facts.statement: A page can load its own CSS and JS without touching other pages, via overrides/main.html; mkdocs.yml extra_css/extra_javascript are global
facts.evidence: The base template (zensical/templates/base.html:82-89, 282-287) renders extra_css then {% block extrahead %}, and the bundle plus extra_javascript inside {% block scripts %}. In scratch I added '{% if page.meta.demo %}<link ...demo.css>' to main.html's extrahead and '{% block scripts %}{{ super() }}<script src=... defer>' . Built site/demo/index.html had demo.css and demo.js; site/index.html had neither.

facts.statement: check_design allows a content <button> only if it has data-copy or data-lc-reset AND the lc-btn class
facts.evidence: check_design.py:267-268 (Facts) and 332-342 (button_problems). Prototype with 7 tab, run, OK and Cancel buttons: 'DESIGN demo/index.html: a <button> in the content that is neither a copy nor a clear-filters button' x7. Nothing checks tab semantics or <video>: role=tab, <select>, <input> and <video> passed silently.

facts.statement: check_site validates every href/src file but NOT poster=, and Page.fix_links does not rewrite poster=
facts.evidence: Scratch build: <video poster="assets/demo/media/poster.jpg"> stayed un-rewritten (a 404 at /demo/) and check_site said 0 problems. After changing page.py:268's regex to (href|src|poster) and check_site.py:56's tuple to include 'poster', the poster became ../assets/demo/media/poster.jpg and a deliberately wrong poster was reported '(no such file)'. data-src attributes would match fix_links' \b(href|src) regex (the hyphen is a word boundary) but are not checked by check_site.

facts.statement: Zensical copies video, captions and other static files from docs/ into site/; a data-search-exclude attribute keeps text out of the site search
facts.evidence: Scratch: docs/assets/demo/media/{labconstrictor-overview.mp4,captions.vtt,poster.jpg} appeared in site/assets/demo/media/. Without the attribute search.json indexed 'FileEditViewRun 1 Initialise environment Run matching Ready' from the simulated window; with data-search-exclude on the demo root the entry held only the intro text.

facts.statement: test_code_rules enforces only Python files in scripts/ and tests/ (annotations, docstrings, <=30-line functions, <=300-line files, no catch-all except, no .get(k, default)); JS and CSS have no limit
facts.evidence: tests/test_code_rules.py:119 SOURCES = *.py under scripts and tests. docs/assets/stylesheets/lc.css is already 338 lines and lc.js 113. Current biggest Python files: guides.py 258, pages_apps.py 208, check_design.py 201, tests/test_site.py 271 (so new tests need a new file).

facts.statement: Reachability and menu rules pass for a /demo/ page linked from home
facts.evidence: check_site reach_problems (check_site.py:152-163) follows any href/src in the HTML; the home tile gives 1 click. Scratch run: 'check_site: 39 pages, 0 problems'. Unlisted mode adds noindex, nofollow to /demo/ automatically (main.html:14) and robots.txt disallows all; write_sitemap lists every real index.html when LISTED is true, so /demo/ joins the sitemap automatically at launch.

facts.statement: Baseline of the unmodified repository builds and passes offline
facts.evidence: Scratch copy: build_site.py (1.7 s), zensical build --strict, write_sitemap, finish_site, check_site (38 pages, 0 problems), check_design (38 pages, 0 problems), 71 unit tests OK. Site is 23 MB in 102 files (21 MB is docs-img, five GIFs total about 18.0 MB); HTML total 0.6 MB; home index.html is 16 KB.

facts.statement: GitHub Pages limits: published site <= 1 GB, repository recommended <= 1 GB, soft bandwidth 100 GB/month, deployment timeout 10 minutes
facts.evidence: WebFetch of docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/github-pages-limits. The page states no per-file limit; GitHub's separate 100 MB per-file push block is general knowledge, not re-fetched here (unverified). The workflow also uploads site/ as a 14-day artifact on pull requests (.github/workflows/publish.yml).

facts.statement: Measured size of a 121 s 1080p/720p H.264 clip made from the real napari, Fiji, notebook and NucleiSky screenshots
facts.evidence: Pessimistic proxy (continuous slow zoom on all frames plus crossfades, CRF 26, medium preset): 1080p 12.3 MB (about 815 kbps), 720p 8.2 MB (about 540 kbps). Typical-screencast proxy (static frames, moving cursor, crossfades): 1080p 3.2 MB (about 215 kbps), 720p 1.8 MB (about 120 kbps). AAC 64 kbps mono for 121 s = 1.0 MB. Encoding times on 4 cores: 107 s (1080p) and 63 s (720p). Source screenshots are only about 1000-1800 px wide, so real captures would be sharper than this proxy. Python's http.server on :8765 has no HTTP Range support; GitHub Pages does, so seeking must be tested on a real deploy or a Range-capable server.

facts.statement: Demo image weight from the existing fixture output
facts.evidence: Scratch fixture_out: ref.png 1.2 MB, query.png 116 KB, overlay_gt_800.png 404 KB (PNG); as optimised JPEG at about 1000 px they would be roughly 150-300 KB each (estimate, not measured). Estimated demo total without video: 0.7-1.2 MB. With a 3-12 MB video the site grows from 23 MB to about 27-37 MB.

facts.statement: Home page and llms.txt need only small edits
facts.evidence: pages_site.page_home (pages_site.py:46-67) has hard-coded sections; llms.py:18-24 has a hard-coded Pages list (new line needed). Zensical validated a link such as ../../demo/index.md from a hand-written guide (content/guides/using-apps.md uses ../../apps/index.md the same way).

facts.statement: A narrow check_design extension works and does not leak to other pages
facts.evidence: Prototype scripts/check_design_demo.py (72 lines, in the scratch repo) plus 3 changed lines in check_design.py: controls with data-demo-act (site-level) or data-demo-sim (inside a simulated window), type=button, are allowed only on a page that has a data-demo root; sim buttons are exempt from the lc-btn-class rule. It reported 0 problems on the good page and caught: video without controls, autoplay, no poster, a tab controlling no panel, two selected tabs, and a sim button on /ecosystem/. 71 existing tests still pass and the new files satisfy test_code_rules.

findings: ## Verdict A /demo/ page, a video and a homepage tile fit the site without a new framework. Nothing needs bypassing. Six rules need small, explicit changes, listed below. I proved the mechanism end to end in a scratch copy of the repo; the real repo was not touched. The scratch copy is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/a3a6ac4f-1857-5992-b7c5-06332778d500/scratchpad/demo-feasibility/site-fit/w2`. There is also an older `site-fit/{repo,work,tpl,dsrc,venv}` left by an earlier stopped run; ignore it. ## Rules that need an explicit, narrow change 1. **Page-specific CSS/JS** (overrides/main.html). Add a front-matter list, for example `page_css`/`page_js`, which main.html loops over: CSS in `{% block extrahead %}`, JS as `{% block scripts %}{{ super() }}
risks: Poster path bug: without the page.py and check_site.py poster fix, a relative poster is silently broken on /demo/ (reproduced) and no check fails.

The check_design exemption could leak: it must be bound to a data-demo root and tested for a page that lacks the root (done in the prototype). Weakening the lc-btn style rule globally would be a real regression.

Markdown raw-HTML mode: a window partial with several top-level siblings separated by blank lines and indentation can turn into a code block; require one balanced root per window and add a test that no <pre> appears.
Heading order and image rules apply to static window HTML: h-tags inside a simulated window can skip levels or add an extra h1; empty-alt decorative fails in main. Use p/CSS/inline SVG for chrome.

Page.write applies decorate_links and fix_links over the entire page body, so any href/src/poster text inside window markup or JSON is rewritten; keep JSON in `<script type=application/json>` with no `src="` strings.
Search pollution: without data-search-exclude the simulated menus (File Edit View) enter search.json.

The demo page is not in the Docs sidebar, yet highlights Docs; reviewers may see that as a break of 'every guide page shows the same sidebar'. Needs the explicit DESIGN.md wording above, or the narrow demo may be placed inside a guide (then only about 930 px wide at 1280 px, too narrow for napari).

Video weight is driven by motion: continuous zoom/pan on every frame costs about 4x a mostly-static screencast (12.3 vs 3.2 MB at 1080p). The production plan should restrain motion, as the spec already says.
Git history growth from re-encoding the MP4 repeatedly; also 14-day PR artifacts upload site/ each build.
Local preview server lacks Range support, so seek bugs may appear only in preview, not on Pages.
No JS/CSS line-limit enforcement exists, so file sizes of the three windows' CSS and JS depend on convention only; lc.css (338) already exceeds 300.
If navigation.instant is ever enabled, a page-specific script will not re-run on navigation.
recommendations: Use one cohesive authored folder content/demo/ (windows partials, JS, CSS, media, example.json, README) copied to docs/assets/demo/ by pages_demo/demo_media, with 'demo' and 'assets/demo' added to GENERATED, .gitignore, README and AGENTS.md.

Generate /demo/ with pages_demo.py using Page(layout='wide', menu='guides/', title equal to the h1, description from data/demo.yaml, edit_url to data/demo.yaml, page_css/page_js lists, jsonld optional) and have overrides/main.html load per-page assets from front matter.

Keep the three simulated windows as static HTML partials, one balanced root each; keep data in example.json and bind it in JS; keep the page useful without JS (first state plus static result image and links to the guides).
Make the narrow checker change as data-demo-act / data-demo-sim, bound to a data-demo root, in a new check_design_demo.py, with tests for good and bad pages; do not touch the lc-btn rule otherwise.
Fix poster handling in page.py and check_site.py and add a test.
Single source for words: data/demo.yaml feeds the tile, page, llms.txt and the Use-an-app link; the transcript is derived from the .vtt; the tile image is derived from the poster.

Add the demo as a new home band (card = one link) after the comic, and one sentence in content/guides/using-apps.md linking ../../demo/index.md; do not add a sixth top-menu entry. Add a Use-hub card only if hubs.py gains a local-picture source.
Video: target 720p H.264, CRF 26-28, preset slow, AAC 64 kbps mono, faststart, preload=none, restrained zoom; budget 3-5 MB, cap 10-15 MB, enforced by a size check in the build.
Write the DESIGN.md and AGENTS.md changes (see findings) in the same pull request as the code, as the repository rule requires.
Add a cheap test that .gitignore covers every GENERATED path, since the inventory is currently kept by hand in four places.
open_questions: Should the demo highlight Docs and show the crumb '<- Docs' (recommended), or should it be placed under the Use track (then its back link is '<- Use an app' and it needs a hubs.py picture source)?
Should the Use hub get a card (requires a code change in hubs.py) or is the using-apps guide link plus the home tile enough?
Should video and demo assets be kept in git or published from a release or other storage? GitHub Pages and the one-workflow build currently assume everything is in the repository.
1080p or 720p for the final video: depends on how much real motion the captured screens contain; this needs the actual capture before it can be settled.
Are narration audio and its voice available? That affects whether the page can claim a narrated video and the AAC budget (about 1 MB at 64 kbps mono).
